reasons: Claimed status is compliant-by-absence; no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and the proposal correctly makes zero edits, which is the minimal correct action.

Cited paragraphs support the rationale: § 3(b) (p0014) imposes substantiation obligations on Contractor toward Company, and § 1(c) (p0007) subjects Contractor personnel to Company's system access/security policies — neither grants Contractor any audit, inspection, verification or system-access right against Customer.

Absence of any audit right binding Customer is at least as protective as the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access), so no negotiation issue should be raised; opening the point risks creating a right that does not exist.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is an expected artifact of compliance-by-absence — there is no audit clause for frequency/notice/cost limits to attach to — and is not evidence of a defect.
Comment accuracy is not at issue (no comment emitted); rationale is internally consistent and notes the time-and-materials billing model leaves no usage metric for a vendor audit to police.
